title: Project Sign era begins
body: The first modern sighting wave reaches Canada. Wartime security apparatus in both Canada and the United States is already watching the sky.

title: Project Magnet starts
body: The Department of Transport lets engineer Wilbert Smith research, part time, whether UFOs could ride Earth's magnetic field. Smith later sets up a UFO observatory outside Ottawa and launches a balloon over the city to watch for reports. The project is terminated in 1954.

title: Project Second Storey
body: The Defence Research Board forms a committee to look at flying saucers crossing Canadian territory as reported by the armed services. It is chaired by the NRC astronomer Dr. Peter Millman.

title: A standing reporting instruction
body: Joint Chiefs of Staff issue communication instructions for reporting vital intelligence sightings from airborne and waterborne sources - the ancestor of the mandatory pilot reports that run for decades. Secondary sources date this instruction to 1954; the designation usually given for it, JANAP 146(C), could not be confirmed against a primary document here.

title: The federal file opens
body: One of the earliest documents in the National Defence UFO file is dated to the mid-1950s; a commonly cited date is 24 November 1957, which this project could not confirm against a primary document. The Library and Archives Canada collection runs from 1947 to the early 1980s, about 9,500 digitized documents.

title: Two cases that stuck
body: 20 May, Falcon Lake, Manitoba: Stefan Michalak is burned by a disc. 4 October, Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia: an object goes into the water and is never found. Defence still identifies the Falcon Lake case as unsolved, and has never said the same about Shag Harbour.

title: The NRC takes over
body: On the recommendation of the Minister of National Defence, responsibility for UFO reports transfers to the National Research Council, which runs the file into the 1990s.

title: Maritime reports accumulate
body: An RCMP report on a Halifax County sighting of 9 December 1970 lands in the NRC's Herzberg Institute file - one of many Atlantic records that were filed and then forgotten.

title: Gander
body: Two nights of airborne encounters over Newfoundland, with a Cessna at 5,000 ft and a Capital Airlines DC-8 both reporting an object; the file is copied to the NRC's Upper Atmosphere Research Section in Ottawa.

title: The Labrador run
body: Reports move up the Labrador coast through late 1978 - Clarenville, Gander, St. Anthony - with police and radar involved in at least one of them.

title: Montreal: forty witnesses at the Bonaventure
body: On 7 November 1990, roughly forty people on the rooftop pool of the Bonaventure Hotel watched for three hours as eight to ten lights in a ring projected beams downward. Air traffic control confirmed no radar contact. Several witnesses were professionals and journalists. It is one of the better-sourced Canadian civilian cases outside the two 1967 events.

title: The file closes
body: NRC collection ends. For decades there is no federal body collecting public UAP reports at all, and pilots still file mandatory occurrence reports into CADORS with no analysis.

title: Yukon: a row of lights
body: At least 31 people in four separate locations across the Yukon reported a row of lights — described by several witnesses as a structure — on the same December night in 1996. The Sky Canada Project report names it among Canada's notable historical encounters. Contemporary documentation is thin; Chris Rutkowski covered it in his survey records.

title: CBC marks the 34th year at Shag Harbour
body: CBC produces the first substantial television documentary revisiting the 1967 Shag Harbour case, interviewing first responders and the researcher who had been tracking the file for decades. It is the beginning of an annual cycle of Shag Harbour coverage that runs through 2017 and beyond — the case becoming more prominent in the archive as the original witnesses age.

title: Harbour Mille: objects over Fortune Bay
body: On 25 January 2010, an RCMP officer and other Harbour Mille residents watch two or three luminous objects rise from Fortune Bay and climb into the night sky. The DND confirms it has no information; French naval presence in the area is raised and denied. The case prompts House of Commons correspondence and receives national media coverage.

title: CIRVIS
body: Vital-information sighting reports continue to be filed by pilots, air traffic controllers and crews, and are released as a ten-year compilation in 2021 through an access-to-information request.

title: North Atlantic CIRVIS reports
body: The 2010–2019 CIRVIS compilation (released by ATI in 2021) includes a cluster of vital-information sighting reports relayed through JRCC Halifax between 2016 and 2018. At least one involved a Lynx helicopter crew reporting an unidentified contact; the incident is in the same file as the Stephenville 2013 event. No analysis was published.

title: Library and Archives Canada publishes the podcast
body: The LAC Discover podcast runs a two-part episode on the Falcon Lake case with Stan Michalak, Chris Rutkowski and Palmiro Campagna, drawing directly on the archived files.

title: Yukon
body: NORAD downs an object at 40,000 feet over central Yukon after Canadian and US aircraft are scrambled. A third interception in a week; the RCMP recovers debris.

title: Question 3227
body: MP Larry Maguire tables a written question asking how many unidentified objects have been tracked since January 2023, referring to the Yukon intercept as "UAP 23".

title: Sky Canada Project
body: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor publishes Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in Canada - 59 pages, 14 recommendations, and a recommendation that a federal department be named to hold the file.

title: The question goes unanswered
body: Written Question 3227, on the Yukon intercept, sat unanswered until the 44th Parliament dissolved. The Library of Parliament now marks it as historical information the government is no longer required to answer.

title: Sixty years, still a visitor centre
body: The Shag Harbour UFO Incident Society keeps the interpretive centre on Highway 3 open, and the case still draws an annual gathering. The first caller, Laurie Wickens, died in 2026 at 76.

title: Written Question 1320
body: MP asks for a five-year breakdown of UAP incidents in Canada — by month, with location, summary and cause. Question 1320 was tabled 15 June 2026 in the 45th Parliament. Where Question 3227 asked about the Yukon intercept, this one asks for the full dataset. No answer has been filed.

title: The United States acts; Canada does not
body: The US DoD's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), established July 2022, published its UAP Historical Record Report in two volumes in 2024, covering reported encounters from 1945 to 2024. The UAP Disclosure Act (December 2023) authorises further declassification of federal records. No Canadian equivalent has followed: the Sky Canada Project's first recommendation — name a federal department to hold the file — remains unimplemented.
